# RenderDragon Partner Program

> Invite-only access to the RenderDragon asset catalog and to "Sign in with RenderDragon" (OAuth 2.1). Partners read assets and authenticate RenderDragon users inside their own apps.

RenderDragon is a free resource library and toolset for Minecraft creators. Partners get two things: a read-only asset API, and an OAuth 2.1 sign-in provider. Access is granted by invitation; request it through the contact page.

## Asset API

- Base URL: `https://api.codersoft.xyz`
- Auth: every request carries an HMAC-SHA256 signature. No cookies, no bearer tokens.
- Read-only. Partners never write to the catalog.

Signed request headers: `x-auth-client`, `x-auth-timestamp` (unix seconds, within 300s), `x-auth-nonce` (random, one use), `x-auth-signature`. Send a `User-Agent`; requests without one are blocked at the edge.

The signature is hex HMAC-SHA256 of this string, newlines included:

```
v1
<METHOD>
<PATH?QUERY>
<CLIENT_ID>
<TIMESTAMP>
<NONCE>
<SHA256_HEX(BODY)>
```

Endpoints (GET):

- `/all` returns every category and asset.
- `/categories` returns the category list.
- `/category/:name` returns one category.
- `/mcicons` returns Minecraft icons.
- `/fonts` returns fonts.
- `/__version` is public and returns a catalog hash for caching.

An asset looks like `{ id, title, credit, filename, ext, url, size, subcategory }`. Show `credit` when it is set.

## Sign in with RenderDragon

- Protocol: OAuth 2.1 authorization code with PKCE.
- Issuer: `https://bmywdrwjdqmrkafhiuwn.supabase.co/auth/v1`
- Authorize: `<issuer>/oauth/authorize`
- Token: `<issuer>/oauth/token` (confidential clients authenticate with HTTP Basic)
- Keys: `<issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json`
- Scopes: `profile`, `email`, `favourites:read`

Flow: redirect the user to `/oauth/authorize` with a PKCE `code_challenge`, they approve on RenderDragon, you receive a code at your redirect URI, then exchange it at `/oauth/token` for an access token and a refresh token.

With Supabase: add RenderDragon as a custom OAuth provider in your Supabase project using the issuer above, then call `supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({ provider: "renderdragon" })`. Your project stores the session like any other provider.

Without Supabase: use any OAuth 2.1 library or plain HTTP against the three endpoints above. Validate access tokens with the JWKS. A public client sends no secret and relies on PKCE.

Users see exactly which fields an app reads before they approve, and can disconnect any app from their RenderDragon account.

## Docs

- [Partner integration guide](https://renderdragon.org/partners/docs): full walkthrough with code for both the API and sign-in.
- [Contact](https://renderdragon.org/contact): request access.
- [Privacy](https://renderdragon.org/privacy)
- [Terms](https://renderdragon.org/tos)

## Notes

- Invite-only. There is no self-serve signup.
- One organization maps to one OAuth app.
- Keep the API secret server-side. It is shown once when you create the key.
- Rate limits are per key. Cache with `/__version` to stay under them.
